title: Manuel Perez, Joe Oliver and Freddie Keppard
summary: He describes Perez as a good reader, recalls first meeting Oliver at Rampart Street, and calls Keppard a gifted but non-reading player.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Do you remember Manuel Perez? Oh yeah. What kind of stuff did he play?
He was good musician. Good musician. Good reader, you know. He was loud too, you know. He liked to blow loud.
He played a sweeter tone than Bradley, I guess, did he?

Well, he had a little bit of tone, yeah, because he was taught, you know. He was a good teacher, you know. After he knew the fundamentals, you know, up to the horn, you know. Do you remember Joe Oliver? Well Joe come up, just like those other fellas, you know, starting out like that. I remember when I first saw him, I was playing with that Eagle band then. And we was playing on Rampart Street one night, just the trombones and the violin and the guitar and bass. So he came in this place with his horn, you know, that's the first time I saw him, first time Dukes and I saw him too. So he asked us to let him play, you know. So he played with us, you know, and made it all right with tunes that he knew, you know. And from then on Dukes was to hire him now and then, and to play with the band, you know. And eventually he started playing around in Storyville, you know, and playing with the brass band, playing with fellas like Perez and them, well they'd help him, you see. He would kind of coach him and he would learn a lot for free, you know. He was free schooling, you know.
Do you remember much about Freda Cuppert? I remember about Freda.

He was a, first he started on the violin, see, picking, you know. And then he picked up the trumpet, see. Well he was a loud trumpet player too. Well he played good too, you know what I'm saying? But he wasn't much in reading, you know, but he could play, you know what I'm saying? He had kind of a gift, you know what I'm saying? Something like Bechet, you know, gifted, you know.
